newsitem.title: UK: Zimbabwe's Mugabe sees average 5 pct growth to 200.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's Mugabe sees average 5 pct growth to 200.

text.p: Zimbabwe President Robert Mugabe on Wednesday said economic growth in the country is expected to average five percent up to the turn of the century.
Speaking at a conference organised by the Confederation of British Industries, Mugabe said the economy was on a firmly positive growth path after expanding by 8.1 percent in 1996.
Analysts see growth of 4.9 to six percent this year.
He said the government was committed to reducing the budget deficit, which came in at 10.1 percent of GDP last year against a targeted 6.7 percent.
Zimbabwe has set a 1997 budget deficit target of 8.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).

He said that tied to the deficit reduction programme was the task of commercialising and privatising public enterprises. But he said investors should not be concerned about government holdings in the economy.
"We feel that the whole area, 99.99 percent, is private (and) is already gaping for investment," Mugabe said in response to questions.

Mugabe said a recent downward trend in interest rates and inflation was likely to continue. Interest rates have fallen to about 26 percent from 40 percent in 1994, and inflation in January stood at 15.8 percent from 28.04 percent a year earlier. -- Andrew Gill, London newsroom +171 542 5887
